cells.tense: The fire is burning steady here, and the people close to you can feel it — you are growing in front of them, not away from them.
cells.ask: Show one of them something today half-finished — a sketch, a wrong turn, a plan that is not right yet. Let the doing be the whole point, not the outcome.
cells.core:
You start things and you mean them. There is a pull that brings friends along without selling anything to them, and you can feel it when someone stands closer because you stood up. That is what it looks like when your own bright patch is grown up and standing in the open — the fire reaching the people in the room, not just the work.

Stay in the open with them and let them answer back in their own language. The loudest one in the room is still you, and you do not need to outshine what comes back. Something said plainly, like this is building and it is not finished yet, is the kind of thing a friend can hold, and it can be handed over without ceremony.

cells.tense: You are already a few steps past where you are, lit up with what this will look like once it lands, and the people with you are still catching their breath.
cells.ask: Say the honest version of where the idea actually stands before the version on the way. One sentence to one person — not a pitch, just the real state of it.
cells.core:
What is happening is that the fire is outrunning the people near you. You are already living inside a version that has not happened, and the interest is real, but the timing has slipped ahead of your feet. When someone asks how it is going, you answer from the future and the present goes missing between you.

The shine is coming from force, not from growth. What works is curiosity you practice out loud — what they think, what they see, whether the thing is even good — and then letting that land and stay. Wherever you find yourself selling, you have already skipped a few of the steps between the idea and the room you are standing in.

cells.tense: The bright one in the room is not the one you are being, and you have been the steady one for a while now, keeping the work close.
cells.ask: Pick something you can actually finish small, do it weekly, and let one friend see it grow. Four minutes on a Tuesday is enough.
cells.core:
What it looks like going well here is someone whose ideas reach the people around them without fanfare — a thing started and shown, a plan that gets a name and a date. You bring real energy to a room when you let yourself, and the people close to you take it in and give it back. That is the ordinary version, not a performance.

What is happening instead is that the showing has gone quiet. The ideas still come, but they stay in drafts and half-thoughts, and the people in the room mostly see you as the steady one. The fire is real and no one hears about it. Starting small and letting one person in is enough to get the current moving again.

cells.tense: You credit the warmth in the room to circumstance or to their good luck, while you are the one who has been raising the temperature.
cells.ask: Look at one thing in the room that is different because of you — a habit, a playlist, a standing thing — and say out loud that you started it.
cells.core:
What it looks like going well here is someone whose energy shows up in the people around them and who owns it — a mood set, a plan that took, a room that runs warmer because they walked in. That is not vanity. It is just what happens when you let yourself be seen starting things.

Right now you keep giving that credit elsewhere — to the group, to luck, to the fact that people were ready. The people in your life take their energy from you and they would say so if asked. You have not said so yourself. This has been yours the whole time it was happening. Claiming it is not boasting, and it is not taking something away from them.
